guardrails.action: stop the test if the reminder arm exceeds control by more than this, and review the wording
stop the reminder for a group whose rate falls below control by more than this, and tell the data protection officer
guardrails.metric: on-time renewal in each group (channel, holder type)

mde: Below 2 points the late renewals avoided do not cover the cost of the messages and of the complaints they bring.

part1.arms: Control: the standard renewal notice 30 days before expiry, as today. Reminder: the same notice plus one reminder message seven days before expiry. A seeded coin per holder puts half in each arm.
part1.decision: Sahar Al-Wuhaibi decides whether every renewal notice is followed by a reminder message seven days before expiry. If the reminder raises on-time renewal by at least 2 points and no guardrail is crossed, the office adopts it for all permit types. If the effect is smaller, or a guardrail is crossed, the office keeps the standard notice.
part1.hypothesis: Holders who get the reminder renew on time more often than holders who get only the standard notice.
part1.withholding: Nobody loses a service they have today: the control arm gets the current notice. The reminder is untested, so giving it to half of the holders for 28 days is how the office learns whether it helps.

primary.definition: the share of holders who renew on or before the expiry date of the permit named in the notice
primary.name: on-time renewal

stop: The test runs 28 days and ends on the planned date. There is one analysis of the primary metric, at the end. One safety look on day 14 reads the guardrails only. There is no early stop for a good result.
stretch: Two primary metrics give two chances of a win. The decision rests on on-time renewal alone; counter visits are reported to help explain the result, whatever they show.
